title: Streaming proxy adapter for function-call-safe JSON envelope negotiation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight streaming proxy adapter that normalizes server-sent HTTP streams into a small, verifiable JSON envelope contract so downstream clients (SDKs, proxies, and third-party HTTP intermediaries) can safely resume, parse structured outputs, and preserve function-call atomicity without depending on transport-specific framing.
background: We continue to see production issues caused by variation in intermediary behavior (HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation, proxies that split chunks, client reconnects) leading to partial function-call payloads, duplicated tool invocations, and hard-to-reproduce failures in downstream SDKs. Existing tickets address low-level framing and resume tokens, but we need a compatibility shim that: 1) provides a consistent envelope for structured outputs (chat + function-call), 2) includes small checkpoints that are safe to resume from, and 3) exposes simple backpressure hints for proxies/clients.
proposed_solution: Introduce a proxy-side adapter that wraps each logical output unit into a JSON envelope with the following fields: envelope_id (stable per logical output), seq (incremental within envelope), kind (text | function_call | metadata | checkpoint), body (string | JSON), and signature (short hash). The adapter will: 1) coalesce transport fragments into complete envelope records before emitting to clients; 2) emit checkpoints at configurable intervals containing the latest envelope_id and seq so a reconnect can request resume from a checkpoint token; 3) ensure function_call envelopes are emitted atomically (all seqs for a function_call are grouped under a single envelope and checkpointing won't split them); 4) expose a small negotiation header (X-Redwood-Stream-Protocol: envelope-v1) so clients can opt into this mode while preserving raw streaming mode for backward compatibility.
design_notes:
- We will implement the adapter as a sidecar middleware inside the edge tier so we can gradually enable per-route.
- Checkpoint tokens will be base64(json({envelope_id, seq, timestamp, server_node})) signed with an HMAC key available to the edge and resume endpoints.
- For function-call envelopes, the adapter must wait until the fully serialized function_call payload fits within configurable size (default 128KB) or until an explicit function-call termination marker is seen from the upstream runtime.
- To avoid additional latency for small responses, the adapter will use a micro-batching window (20ms) that coalesces fragments but flushes quickly for low-latency paths.
- The design intentionally keeps envelopes flat and small to remain friendly to proxies and CDNs that may impose line-length or buffering constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Edge adapter produces envelope-v1 stream with valid JSON envelopes separated by newline and a top-level 'end-of-stream' marker
Clients can reconnect and request resume using a checkpoint token; runtime accepts tokens and resumes from specified envelope_id/seq without duplicating function_call execution
Function-call envelopes are not split across checkpoints; partial function_call payloads are not delivered to clients
Benchmark: added adapter introduces <3ms median additional latency for 512B responses and <15ms for 16KB responses in 95th percentile under normal micro-batching settings
Integration tests: simulate proxy chunk-splitting, HTTP/2 stream interleaving and client reconnects; no duplicated tool invocations observed in 1000 simulated reconnect runs
Docs and SDK: negotiation header documented; JS and Python SDKs include a toggle to opt-in to envelope-v1 and to present checkpoint/resume APIs

2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Spoke with SDK owners — they prefer an explicit header negotiation instead of content sniffing. Adding negotiation header to design.
2025-02-14 Marcus Nguyen: Found that several CDN configs buffer long lines; decided to keep newline-delimited JSON with explicit checksum to avoid single very long lines.
2025-02-17 QA: Added test plan to simulate lossy chunks and concurrent reconnects; initial failures were due to unsigned checkpoint expiry — moved to HMAC-signed tokens with TTL.
2025-02-19 Security review: walkthrough performed; HMAC key rotation must be supported by edge; follow-up ticket suggested for key rotation tooling (ENG-521815).

2025-02-20 Marcus Nguyen: Prototype deployed to staging behind a feature flag for the /v1/chat/stream endpoint. Observability hooks added to track resume success rate and function-call duplication events.
